speaker: Jonathan Awad
en: was like, is this on the chain? Is this on chain? I was like, no, it's not on chain. We went way more difficult. Not difficult. That's not true. There's no juxtaposition. It was just not on chain. We filed a brand new security, Reg D security, SEC finner registered. We're a licensed broker dealer and we were trading app. So it was like, we're JP Morgan, Robin Hood, NASDAQ in one, basically. And we created a brand new security and it was a licensed, like an ATS. So that's for alternative trading system. Instead of NASDAQ, which is a stock exchange, we did an ATS. There's only 12 licensed ATSs in the world. And we tried to just IPO buildings. zh: 会问，这是 on chain 的吗？这是上链的吗？我说，不，不是上链的。我们走了一条难得多的路。不是说难得——那不对。这没有什么对比。只是没上链而已。我们申报了一种全新的证券，Reg D 证券，SEC finner 注册。我们是持牌 broker dealer，而且我们是交易平台。所以基本上就像，我们是 JP Morgan、Robin Hood、NASDAQ 三合一。而且我们创造了一种全新的证券，它是持牌的，像一个 ATS。ATS 是指另类交易系统。不同于作为证券交易所的 NASDAQ，我们做的是 ATS。世界上只有 12 家持牌 ATS。我们试图直接 IPO 大楼。我说“尝试”，我们 IPO 了四栋楼，融了大约 3000 万美元。这样你就能买一栋楼的一部分，就像你能买一家公司的一部分一样。只是后来 COVID 来了，摧毁了商业地产。而且在 COVID 之后很难再融到钱。我们本来在谈 Series B，然后我们最终卖掉了公司。我是首席投资官。我不是 CEO。所以我没有真正获得那种经验。我没有那么多管理经验。我没有那么多“我们怎么赚钱”的经验。所以，我是一个首次当 CEO 的二次创业者。对于任何处于那种“接近但不是 CEO”

en: the CEO's job is to deal with all of the problems. If something's going well, you don't really want to focus on it as much. You want to hire amazing people to go and make it even better. zh: CEO 的工作就是处理所有的问题。如果某件事进展顺利，你不那么想专注于它。你想雇出色的人去把它做得更好。你只需要专注于问题。所以所有问题都来找你。所以当我做首席投资官时，我有一个我专注和处理的领域，但我不必处理其他团队的人事问题。我不必处理其他团队的牌照申报，或者营销的事情，或者“我们这儿怎么办？”，嘿，竞争对手是不是这么定价的？或者，嘿，网站应该长什么样？网站文案是其中最有意思的之一，看起来不难，但其实是极其难的挑战。而且你必须非常有创造力，必须深思熟虑。有太多事情可能出难题或出错，而 CEO 要处理，其他每一个人都不用。之所以我的 CTO，我们的 CTO，Tim，Timothy Hyde，致敬，我最好的朋友，了不起的人，真正的天才。我们合作如此顺畅的原因是，我们完全把公司一分为二，工程以及所有相关的，产品执行以及所有相关的，设计执行以及所有相关的，都归他，我和这些完全不沾边。我甚至没有我们 GitHub 的访问权限。作为一个 CEO，我觉得这么说很搞笑。我一直觉得很好笑。这现在已经有点像个内部笑话了，因为我用不着权限，我又不会往 prod 推代码，他们也不想让我推。然后我处理其他一切。所以我们配合得这么好。虽然我也会发表意见，高层次的，但也不算真的参与。就是这样截然不同。

COVID had just hit. You know, it was 2021 and there was this massive transformation in financial services where folks, when I say folks, I mean banks, lenders, payments companies, folks. Financial services before could rely on face-to-face, coming to my branch, coming to my company. I know you. I see you. I can onboard you. In COVID, 2020, they didn't do that. PPP, so many hundreds of billions of dollars was handed out in the Paycheck Protection Program. So all these businesses were applying online for the first time. All these banks were decisioning for the first real time. And no matter what any financial services company says to you, very few, even the really big ones, were doing that much digitally. And for the most part, it was really just like the top 10. Not even the top 10. Some scattering, smattering of the top 10 had a bunch of digital. Very little, actually, like half the top 10 didn't. When I say top 10 banks, lenders, payments companies, and then most of the rest was just, weren't relying on digital as much. And then they had to. And so that was this humongous moment, basically, of massive transformation in the industry. And I was at a company that was doing pretty well. And I learned a lot really fast. And there's just so many ideas that were constantly coming because they kept asking. You have that many signed deals. I'm talking to hundreds and hundreds more, obviously, right? Like, even at a 40% win rate over time, you're still dealing and juggling. I probably juggled 400 or 500 deals over the course of that, those 12 months, which sounds crazy. And it is. It was the most I ever worked besides Baselayer. It was like that and then Baselayer. And they just gave me so many ideas and they asked so many questions and they literally like, hey, can you do this? Can you do this? Can you do this? And so I took a bunch of them and I brought it internal and I was like, hey, like, I wrote up PRDs. I have all these customers who want it. Like, this is how we source the data and the product, et cetera. And I got a lot of no's. Hey, you're in sales. They in sales. And I was like, okay, that's kind of not good enough for me. One of our mutual best friends, I met him in high school, went to Bronx High School of Science in New York. Shout out to Bronx Science. And he went to Columbia as well. Our friend Andrew, so Tim's a co-founder, Andrew. Andrew's a CS engineer and then after was an engineer for a bit, became a DJ. Like a really good one too. He's pretty popular. And we met out one night, myself, Tim, and we were just with Andrew. And then I was just like ranting and raving about some startup ideas I had in 2022. And Tim, we're in the back of a yellow cab and Tim's just asking a question, question, question. I was like, who are you? These are amazing questions. And Tim's just this awesome, super cool, like very tall, awesome guy. And he was like, oh, CTO of a machine learning company. He just sold to Snapchat two years ago. And I'm getting kind of bored. I'm getting antsy. Like I want to do something. I'm like, amazing. Let's start a company. And he looks at me.
